observations: Both readers made the same error in the pittum: they added the repeats 'שבעים שבעים' and 'ששה עשר ששה עשר', and in Rabbi Natan they printed היטיב twice. This printing has each word once. These look like the readers normalizing to a remembered text, so agreement between them is not proof here.
Both readers' בֹּטֵחַ is also a normalization. The page has the plene בּוֹטֵחַ.

Every repeated occurrence was checked separately, with no global substitution. בִּכְלִי has a single hiriq dot at all 6 occurrences (mishnah 1, 2, 3, 4b and 5). שְׁיָרֵי appears 3 times with the same visible shape. שֶׁלַּמִּזְבֵּחַ appears twice with patah. The forms שׁוֹפֵךְ in mishnah 1–2 and שֹׁפֵךְ in mishnah 3, and חֲצוֹת in mishnah 3, 6 and 8 against חֲצֹת in mishnah 5, are genuine differences in the printing.

Numbers 28:9–10 is the only passage with te'amim. The verse-end mark has the same shape as the ordinary colon, so it is transcribed as ':'. If the project prefers U+05C3 for verse ends, that is an encoding choice, not something the print decides.
Mishnah number letters (א–ח) and the Ana acrostics are kept out of the recited and study text.
